one_line: Safe, evidence-linked website repair workflow with human-approved patches and verification.
what_it_does: Audits websites, maps findings to source, proposes bounded diffs, obtains approval, applies branch-first changes, and verifies results.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP materially improves reliability through structured audit state, source mapping, approval, apply, and verification rather than UI guessing; the core workflow is agent-centered.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 13 structured tools for scan through compare audits.
Human and agent share audit, diff, approval, applied, and verification state.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent end-to-end repair product with aligned audit, source viewer, diff, approval, and verification surfaces, though no video is supplied.
execution_evidence: Ten gallery images are reported and the about text names concrete dashboard and diff surfaces.
Demo is marked alive and implementation details include deterministic fixes and signed state.
impact_rationale: Website owners and developers have a clear recurring problem—turning audit findings into safe, verifiable fixes—and the workflow addresses the handoff directly.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets website accessibility, performance, SEO, and broken-link repair.
Explicit approval and before/after verification address consequential source changes.
creativity_rationale: The audit-to-authorized-diff-to-proof loop is a fresh, focused synthesis for agent-assisted maintenance.
creativity_evidence: Evidence-linked source hints and bounded branch-first repair are distinctive workflow choices.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow and human approval improve trust; operational setup is not demonstrated in video.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; visual execution is not independently checkable.
standouts: Strong safety and verification framing around actual code edits.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-native workflow and credible product value, with only evidence thinness limiting certainty.

one_line: A shared 3D stage where a human blocks the performer and an agent composes the camera.
what_it_does: Lets a person move a performer while an agent inspects the live scene, evaluates and sets camera positions, and captures takes with revision protection.
leverage_rationale: Shared scene revision state makes agent camera direction collaborative and rejects stale actions; this is difficult to reproduce comparably with generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies inspect, evaluate, set-camera, and capture tools.
Revision-number conflict handling rejects camera moves based on stale human-visible state.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a deliberately small but coherent co-directing loop; gallery and demo are present, but no video evidence or repo is supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and three frame sheets plus two gallery images are listed.
Central workflow and conflict behavior are concretely described.
impact_rationale: Creative practitioners and learners can explore human-agent co-direction in a tangible scene, though the intentionally tiny scene limits breadth.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description identify blocking, camera selection, and shared scene control as the use case.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model—human changes blocking while an agent composes from current scene state—is memorable and unusually well matched to the medium.
creativity_evidence: Co-directing rather than regenerating scenes is the core concept.
Stale-revision rejection turns concurrency into a visible creative interaction.
usability_note: Small scene and clear turn-taking should make the concept legible; depth beyond the experiment is unknown.
red_flags: No video or transcript; functional completion is claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Revision-safe shared scene is an excellent WebMCP interaction idea.
advance_reason: Highly original and genuinely shared agent-human creative state.

one_line: A proof-carrying work layer where agents adversarially test human-owned definitions of done.
what_it_does: Maintains mission contracts, lets agents submit counterexamples, exposes authority and evidence state, and invalidates only proofs affected by later dependency changes.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools enable an agent to inspect contracts and actively challenge them while preserving human semantic authority; this is more than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools include submit_counterexample and bounded human decision requests.
Stateful false-green detection and minimum re-proof planning are described.
execution_rationale: The concept and invariants are coherent, but there are no frame sheets, video, transcript, or public repo to substantiate the claimed workflow.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and the description specifies deterministic evaluation and proof invalidation.
No submitted video or gallery images.
impact_rationale: Teams using agents need trustworthy acceptance criteria and current proof; the audience and problem are concrete even if implementation evidence is thin.
impact_evidence: Description targets false-green completion claims and dependency-driven proof invalidation.
Human authority and auditable evidence directly address trust in agent work.
creativity_rationale: Adversarially challenging the definition of done, rather than merely executing it, is a novel and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: submit_counterexample is positioned as the key product interaction.
Selective re-proof preserves unrelated valid evidence.
usability_note: The authority model sounds clear, but no interface evidence is supplied.
red_flags: No visual or video evidence; execution claims cannot be checked.
standouts: Strong trust model with human-owned semantics and adversarial agent review.
advance_reason: High-concept, high-value agent collaboration despite very thin execution evidence.

one_line: A human-controlled listening simulation with an agent-guided shared session.
what_it_does: Compares synthetic hearing profiles in a family scene, keeps consent and playback human-controlled, and lets an agent summarize observations and propose one bounded change.
leverage_rationale: The agent works against shared live session state and safety boundaries, including consent, profile, playback, observations, and bounded scene changes; agent mode changes the experience rather than merely clicking it.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes Agent Reveal, shared session state, consent, profile selection, and agent-guided comparisons.
About text says the agent transforms the presentation into a new hierarchy and journey.
execution_rationale: This has the strongest packet evidence: a live demo, three-minute video, transcript, repo, and a coherent human-first-to-agent-reveal flow.
execution_evidence: Video is present with 180 seconds and transcript shows session start, consent, profile, playback, and observation.
Demo is alive and public repo is reported.
impact_rationale: People with hearing loss and their families have a specific communication challenge, and an illustrative shared simulation can create empathy without claiming diagnosis.
impact_evidence: Audiology-informed motivation and explicit non-clinical framing.
Family conversation with competing television sound is concretely demonstrated.
creativity_rationale: Turning a human-first hearing illustration into a shared, consent-bounded agent session is a thoughtful and memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent Reveal is a distinct mode rather than an agent silently driving the original UI.
Person retains control while agent proposes a bounded scene change.
usability_note: Consent, volume acknowledgement, and explicit playback grant show careful interaction design.
red_flags: Simulation is illustrative and not a hearing assessment; claims should not exceed that scope.
standouts: Excellent safety framing and end-to-end demonstrated shared session.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed execution, clear impact, and meaningful agent-human collaboration.

one_line: Scoped, stale-state-safe authority and verification for consequential agent transactions.
what_it_does: Turns agent actions into approved exact plans with temporary authority, commit, canonical verification, receipts, and recovery safeguards.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP capability itself becomes conditional on exact human-approved transaction state, making structured agent authority the product rather than an interface convenience.
leverage_evidence: Workflow is Intent to preview to approval to scoped authority to commit to verification and receipt.
Stale plans lose commit authority and require re-planning.
execution_rationale: The protocol description is unusually detailed and coherent, but no video, gallery, repo, or observable evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and many invariants are explicitly listed.
No submitted video or gallery images.
impact_rationale: Consequential web actions need least-privilege authority, stale-state protection, and receipts; the audience and risk are broad and concrete.
impact_evidence: Examples include offboarding, ownership transfer, access revocation, billing, and deletion.
Post-condition verification and audit integrity address real operational failure modes.
creativity_rationale: Making temporary, plan-hash-bound mutation capability a protocol-level property is an ambitious and original agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Mutation tools appear only after exact approval and disappear when authorization is invalid.
usability_note: Exact previews and receipts promise trust, but the UI and workflow are not shown.
red_flags: No visual or video evidence; implementation quality is unverified.
standouts: Strong authority and stale-state model for high-risk agent actions.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and impact potential; execution must be validated in a later stage.

one_line: A structured agent-operated storefront for bundle creation and inventory management.
what_it_does: Provides catalog search, inventory and pricing views, bundle configuration, order workspace, and WebMCP audit tooling.
leverage_rationale: Structured catalog and bundle operations reduce scraping friction and improve repeatability, but a capable general agent could achieve much of the outcome through the visible storefront.
leverage_evidence: About text describes seven registered tools and live configure_bundle execution.
52-product catalog, inventory matrix, and order workspace are exposed.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a broad, coherent commerce demo in the description and five gallery images, but no video or transcript confirms end-to-end behavior.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and five gallery images reported.
Concrete bundle, catalog, pagination, and inventory surfaces are described.
impact_rationale: Retail operators and shoppers can benefit from agent-assisted bundle configuration and safer inventory workflows; the fit is clear though not uniquely urgent.
impact_evidence: Targets store inventory management and custom bundle creation.
Price-elasticity and stock-risk views support procurement decisions.
creativity_rationale: A competent commerce application with a useful WebMCP angle, but the category and interaction model are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Custom bundle configuration and agent audit drawer provide a real new angle.
usability_note: Catalog and preset workflows sound approachable; breadth may increase complexity.
red_flags: No video evidence; gallery claims are packaging-level evidence only.
standouts: Concrete commerce workflow rather than a generic chatbot storefront.
advance_reason: Solid, credible implementation concept with meaningful but not transformative WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A spatial PDF research desk shared by a person and an agent through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Unfolds PDF pages onto a persistent canvas, lets agents inspect, search, focus regions, and present grounded page sequences while preserving reversible shared state.
leverage_rationale: The agent directly manipulates browser-local PDF layout, camera, page identity, and reversible presentation state; generic UI driving would be markedly less reliable and grounded.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows inspect workspace, broad read, and present sequence calls.
Agent targets normalized figure/equation regions and restores prior geometry on exit.
execution_rationale: The video transcript provides a detailed end-to-end demonstration, and the frame sheet visibly supports the PaperSpace UI and Codex/WebMCP workflow, though frames are low-resolution.
execution_evidence: 158-second video with transcript describes a complete grounded introduction flow.
Frame sheet shows PaperSpace, WebMCP, and Codex workflow, with visible limitations in fine detail.
impact_rationale: Researchers, students, and educators have a real problem with linear, context-detached PDF reading; spatial grounding directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Description identifies navigation among related work, methods, equations, figures, experiments, and appendices.
Presentation captions remain anchored to original pages.
creativity_rationale: The spatial reading desk and agent-controlled camera/presentation model are a genuinely original, memorable use of browser-local shared state.
creativity_evidence: Persistent 2D paper desk preserves spatial memory rather than collapsing research into retrieved text.
Reversible camera flights and region-focused presentation pursue the concept deeply.
usability_note: Grounded captions and user interruption/redirect improve control; spatial layouts may have a learning curve.
red_flags: Contact sheet is low-resolution and repetitive, so fine-grained visual state changes are hard to verify.
standouts: Excellent WebMCP-native shared spatial state and grounded presentation workflow.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and creativity with unusually strong demonstrated workflow evidence.

one_line: A private, agent-readable semantic media library that lets users own discovery and recommendation.
what_it_does: Searches a large Internet Archive-derived catalog locally, exposes semantic data and media operations to agents, and supports user-controlled channels and curation without login or ads.
leverage_rationale: Exposing the site's semantic catalog and media operations directly lets agents recommend and curate from authoritative structured state instead of scraping a streaming UI.
leverage_evidence: About text describes approximately 20,000 titles and WebMCP semantic dataset access.
Privacy-preserving in-browser semantic search and agent curation are central to the product.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a substantial, coherent media platform with public repo, live demo, gallery, and frame sheets, but no video transcript or direct observed run.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and three frame sheets plus three gallery images reported.
Concrete catalog, privacy, and channel goals are described.
impact_rationale: Viewers frustrated by fragmented catalogs, ads, surveillance, and opaque recommendations have a clear audience need that user-owned discovery addresses.
impact_evidence: Description identifies no ads, no login, no behavioral data collection, and private local search.
creativity_rationale: Sovereign semantic media discovery with agent-native curation is an ambitious and distinctive alternative to centralized streaming recommendation.
creativity_evidence: Own-your-algorithm thesis combines local privacy, semantic search, and agent-readable media operations.
usability_note: No-login local discovery is attractive; catalog breadth and media playback details are not fully evidenced.
red_flags: No video or transcript; product operation is inferred from text and stills.
standouts: Strong privacy and user-control thesis paired with agent-native data access.
advance_reason: Distinctive product vision with credible audience value and meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A fictional support workboard where agents manage cases through structured, human-approved actions.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents list, open, create, edit, and propose case stage moves while surfacing pending actions for human decision.
leverage_rationale: Structured case tools and pending-action state improve agent reliability over DOM guessing, but the workflow remains comparable to conventional browser automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists list/open/create/update/propose-stage tools.
Agent mutations create visible pending actions rather than silently changing cases.
execution_rationale: The fictional workboard has a coherent described workflow and live demo/public repo, but no gallery, video, or transcript demonstrates it.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repo reported.
Description specifies four stages and human review behavior.
impact_rationale: Support and operations teams have a real intake-to-resolution problem, and a structured shared case record is a credible solution.
impact_evidence: Motivation connects incoming chat requests to assignment, follow-up, and outcome recording.
Case lifecycle covers New, Triage, Investigating, and Resolved.
creativity_rationale: The safety-oriented pending-action layer is useful, but support boards and agent case updates are a familiar category.
creativity_evidence: Fictional post-message workflow and visible human approval provide a modest original angle.
usability_note: Explicit pending actions preserve control; absence of visual evidence limits assessment.
red_flags: No screenshots, video, or transcript beyond packaging screenshot; execution is thinly evidenced.
standouts: Appropriate choice to fictionalize sensitive WhatsApp-derived operational data.
advance_reason: Credible but comparatively familiar concept with insufficient execution evidence for advancement.

one_line: A task board where agents propose new WebMCP tools that require human approval before registration.
what_it_does: Manages tasks and overdue completion signals, and lets agents compose proposed read-only tools while human approval gates registration and writes.
leverage_rationale: The agent can extend its own structured surface, while the API contract and UI approval prevent unreviewed registration or mutation; this is a meaningful capability beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes propose_tool from whitelisted read primitives.
Only human approval triggers registerTool and bulk writes require confirmation.
execution_rationale: The layered concept and safety constraints are coherent, but only one gallery image and no video/repo execution evidence are supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and one gallery image reported.
Description gives concrete task tools, heuristic completion, proposal, and approval flow.
impact_rationale: Teams using agent task boards could gain tailored tools without surrendering control, though the benefit is more experimental than broadly demonstrated.
impact_evidence: Overdue-task completion heuristics address a practical workflow problem.
Human-gated tool creation addresses extensibility and safety.
creativity_rationale: Self-extending agent tools with explicit human approval is a genuinely novel and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tool Forge composes new tools from a whitelist and registers only after a real UI click.
The project explicitly tests whether an agent can propose capabilities without self-authorizing them.
usability_note: Approval gates are understandable, but self-extension adds conceptual complexity and is not visually demonstrated.
red_flags: Very thin visual evidence; the central extension workflow is claimed, not observed.
standouts: Strong safety boundary around dynamic WebMCP registration.
advance_reason: Original, high-leverage concept merits advancement despite execution evidence limitations.
